questions.question: Taking "the ethical point of view" means
options: choosing to sacrifice your own good for the good of someone else
deciding that other people and their core values are worthy of your respect
putting your self-interest above the interests of everyone else
refusing to accept help from other people
abiding by your religious beliefs even when it is difficult

questions.question: An association of people organized under a system of rules designed to advance the good of its members over time is called a
options: government
business
society
monopoly
constitution

questions.question: Rules of conduct describing what people ought and ought not to do in various situations are called
options: morality
virtues
ideals
philosophy
a denominations

questions.question: Ethics is
options: a rational examination of people's moral beliefs
a branch of philosophy
one way to determine which activities are "good" and which are "evil"
a field of study more than 2
All of the above

questions.question: Generally, what does it mean to make an ethical decision?
options: Choosing the option that benefits the individual the most
Making a decision based solely on emotional response
Following the law and societal rules without question
Considering the impact of your actions on the well-being of others

questions.question: How can cultural differences impact ethical perceptions?
options: They have no impact; ethical principles are the same worldwide
Ethics are purely individual and not influenced by culture
Different cultures may prioritize different values leading to varied ethical judgments
Cultural differences make it impossible to have a common ethical ground

questions.question: What is the role of empathy in ethical decision-making?
options: It is irrelevant to ethical considerations
It only applies to personal relationships and not to ethical decisions
It can hinder making rational ethical decisions
It helps understand the perspectives and feelings of others affected by decisions

questions.question: Why is it important to consider the consequences of our actions when making ethical decisions?
options: Consequences are the only factors that determine the ethicality of actions
Considering consequences helps predict and mitigate potential harm
Ethical decisions should be based solely on intentions not consequences
Consequences are irrelevant; what matters is following rules

questions.question: What does the concept of fairness imply in ethical decision-making?
options: Treating everyone the same regardless of circumstances
Giving everyone exactly what they deserve
Maximizing benefits for a few people
Ensuring that decisions do not favor one party over another unjustly

questions.question: How does accountability relate to ethical behavior?
options: It means following orders without questioning them
Accountability is only relevant in legal contexts
It involves ensuring personal gain from ethical decisions
It implies taking responsibility for the consequences of one's actions

questions.question: In what way can ethical dilemmas arise?
options: Ethical dilemmas do not truly exist; there is always a best choice
When there is a clear right and wrong choice
Only in professional settings not in personal life
When there are conflicting ethical principles or values at stake

questions.question: What role does integrity play in ethics?
options: It ensures compliance with laws and regulations
It ensures compliance with the holy books
Integrity is about gaining the approval of your friends
It involves consistently upholding moral principles even when it's challenging

questions.question: What is one of the reasons people live in communities?
options: It allows individuals to specialize and focus on particular activities
People are more prone to external dangers
It helps stay away from personal relationships
Everyone can do all activities without the need to specialize

questions.question: A responsible community member
options: take the needs and desires of only their friends into account when they make decisions
take the needs and desires of other people into account when they make decisions
does not share core values with others
makes decisions that benefits only their friends

questions.question: Chinese scientist He Jiankui announced to the world that he successfully did what?
options: used the gene-editing tool CRISPR-Cas9 to modify the DNA of two embryos before birth
used the gene-editing tool CRISPR-Cas9 to offer custom designer babies as needed by the mother
changed the race of a baby
used the gene-editing tool CRISPR-Cas9 to offer custom designer babies as needed by both parents

questions.question: Josef Mengele was known as
options: the angel of life
the devil of death
the devil of life
the angel of death

questions.question: In class, we discussed how mostly everyone shares "core values" desiring what
options: happiness
beach living
fasting
bull fighting

questions.question: One of the reasons as society has rules is to
options: advance the good of members over time
make sure every person can do what they like
hinder community growth
destroy progress

questions.question: ____ is what people ought / ought not to do in various situations
options: community
morality
philosophy
psycology

questions.question: _____ is a rational examination of morality
options: psycology
philosophy
ethics
community

questions.question: We used _____ in class to learn about how we are wired (in this case our visual system)
options: perceptual illusions
magic
binoculars
a magnifying glass

questions.question: People donate more to ONE named person than to many unnamed people. This has been called the
options: Group Effect
Identifiable Victim Effect
Donation Effect
Identifiable Group Effect

questions.question: Choice aversion in donations is an example of how
options: Morality is defined by technology
Morality is subjective and imperfect
Morality is about financial gains
Ethical theories are based on real experiences

questions.question: ______ is the philosophical study of morality and a rational examination into people's moral beliefs and behavior
options: Theology
Anthropology
Computer Science
Ethics

questions.question: _____ produces persuasive explanation for a skeptical yet open-minded audience
options: Morality
Digital communications
Workable Ethical theory
Society

questions.question: Workable Ethical theories are often used (in computing) to
options: collect requirements
test code
convert algorithm to code
explain algorithms involving human choice

questions.question: What does ethical relativism primarily propose?
options: Moral principles are entirely objective and independent of human perspectives
Moral principles are determined by individual choice
Moral values and principles are relative to the cultural societal or personal context
There are universal moral principles applicable to all cultures

questions.question: According to ethical relativism: when is an action considered morally right?
options: When it aligns with universal moral laws
When it maximizes utility for the greatest number of people
When it conforms to natural law
When it is approved by the majority in a particular society

questions.question: What challenge does relativism pose to moral judgments?
options: It suggests that moral judgments are universally valid
It implies that moral judgments are infallible
It makes moral judgments subjective and potentially varies from one culture to another
It denies the possibility of moral progress

questions.question: Ethical relativism often leads to which of the following conclusions
options: There is one true moral code that all societies should follow
Societies cannot judge the moral practices of other societies
Moral principles should be based on the outcomes they produce
Ethical standards are independent of human beliefs and culture

questions.question: What is the central claim of cultural relativism?
options: Moral truths exist independently of cultural perspectives
Cultural traditions have no influence on the validity of moral principles
All cultures ultimately share the exact same fundamental moral principles
Moral values and practices are valid only within their own cultural context

questions.question: Cultural relativism suggests that:
options: What is considered morally right in one culture can be deemed morally wrong in another
Cultural traditions should not influence moral judgments
Ethics is determined by genetics
There is a single universal moral standard applicable across all cultures

questions.question: Which of the following would be a criticism of cultural relativism?
options: It may prevent moral criticism of harmful practices within a culture
It encourages a deeper understanding of foreign cultures
It can lead to moral absolutism
It overemphasizes the role of reason in moral decision-making

questions.question: According to cultural relativism how should moral disagreements between cultures be approached?
options: Through the lens of one's own cultural moral standards
By understanding and respecting the moral frameworks of the respective cultures
By adopting a universal moral standard to judge all cultures
By assuming that some cultures are more morally advanced than others

questions.question: One of the cons of cultural relativism is that
options: It provides clear guidelines for cultures in conflict
Acknowledges cultural contexts
It accounts for different social contexts that demand different moral guidelines
It doesn't account for evolution of moral guidelines

questions.question: What does the Divine Command Theory propose?
options: Ethical principles are the result of social contracts
Moral values exist independently of divine commands
An action is morally right if it is commanded by God
Morality is determined by rational analysis

questions.question: How does Divine Command Theory resolve moral dilemmas?
options: By consulting divine commands as revealed in sacred texts
Through democratic consensus
By referring to natural laws
By applying utilitarian principles

questions.question: Which of the following is a criticism of Divine Command Theory?
options: It enhances moral autonomy by encouraging individual moral reasoning
It fails to recognize the diversity of religious beliefs
None of the above
It asserts that morality is arbitrary depending on God's will

questions.question: Divine Command Theory primarily emphasizes the role of:
options: Individual conscience in moral decision-making
God's will in determining the morality of actions
Logical reasoning in ethics
Cultural norms and values

questions.question: What is the main principle of ethical egoism?
options: An action is morally right if it primarily benefits the individual making the decision
Actions are morally right if they promote the greatest good for the greatest number
Moral principles are inherent in the nature of the universe
Morality is determined by the expectations of society

questions.question: Ethical egoism advocates that:
options: Altruism is the basis of moral action
Personal well-being is the ultimate moral aim
Ethical decisions should be made without considering personal consequences
Individuals have a moral obligation to serve others

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios exemplifies ethical egoism?
options: Sacrificing personal interests for the welfare of the group
Sharing user data without consent to paid advertisers
Following laws and social norms
Donating to charity online

questions.question: A criticism of ethical egoism is that it:
options: Leads to a lack of concern for the well-being of others
Encourages too much altruism
Is too difficult to apply in real-world situations
Undermines personal freedom and autonomy

questions.question: Kantian ethics is based on:
options: The inherent evil in people
The principle of utility
The consequences of actions
The intention behind the action and adherence to duty

questions.question: Which of the following is a key component of Kant's Categorical Imperative?
options: Act to maximize the overall happiness
Act only according to that maxim whereby you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law
Follow the holy books
Treat others as means to an end

questions.question: Alex decides to return a lost wallet because he believes it is his duty to do so regardless of any reward. According to Kantianism is Alex's action morally commendable?
options: No because he did not consider the happiness his action would bring
Yes because he acted out of duty with no regard for personal gain
Yes because returning the wallet maximizes social welfare
No because he should have kept the wallet to benefit himself

questions.question: Jamie tells the truth to a friend even though it may hurt the friend's feelings. Kantianism would view Jamie's action as:
options: Morally wrong since it would not benefit society
Morally right if the intention was to respect the principle of honesty as a universal duty
Morally right since it would benefit only Jamie
Morally wrong since it does not prioritize the friend's happiness

questions.question: According to Kantianism: You may claim credit for code written by someone else
options: No since the proposed moral rule is self-defeating
No since it is not a divine commans
Yes since it increases overall happiness
Yes since the universal rule is logical

questions.question: Which of the following is a workable ethical theory?
options: Kantianism
Divine Command theory
Egoism
Cultural relativism

questions.question: The Trolley Problem is commonly used in ethics to explore which moral issue?
options: The role of emotions in political decision-making
Choosing between saving more people (utilitarianism) or following moral rules
How laws determine right and wrong behavior
Whether moral decisions should be based on personal benefit
